Tabs owns widget state, key handling and bar animation (tabs.py:269-270 reactives, tabs.py:321-328 watcher, tabs.py:330-363 key handling).

UnderlineBar owns click-span attachment via @click metadata (underline_bar.py:90-94), the same mechanism scrollbar.py:113-114 already uses.

Reuses existing extension points: layout_resolve (tabs.py:166), Opacity for inactive labels (tabs.py:209-212), UnderlineBar for the bar (tabs.py:222), Widget.animate for bar movement (tabs.py:~324), and the existing @click action dispatch to action_range_clicked (tabs.py:211, 435).

Defines a private _Edge (tabs.py:55-69) instead of reusing _layout_resolve.Edge. The base Edge is a Protocol with class-attribute defaults (base _layout_resolve.py:13-18) that cannot be instantiated; the reference converted it to a NamedTuple. _Edge satisfies the same duck-typed contract without touching the shared module, so this is a reasonable alternative and not a parallel layout path.

opacity.py:36-43 now yields style + Style.from_color(color=blended), so the Opacity renderable keeps attributes and click metadata instead of discarding them (base opacity.py:36-42 rebuilt a bare style).
The fix matches the reference's style + color_style approach (reference opacity.py:36-42).
Widget code builds only public renderables (Text, Opacity, UnderlineBar) and does not reach into rich internals beyond the Text and Style API.
async def on_key (tabs.py:330) matches the base convention (widget.py:356, widgets/_tree_control.py:276).
Google-style Args docstrings match underline_bar.py's existing docstring style.
Tests sit at tests/test_tabs.py beside tests/test_widget.py and similar root-level test files, and use tests.utilities.render.render as tests/renderables/test_underline_bar.py does.

Nit only, not a failure: tabs.py:267 sets can_focus = True in the class body, whereas base widgets use the class keyword form (widgets/_placeholder.py:20). It is redundant because Widget.__init_subclass__ already defaults can_focus to True (widget.py:82).
Inactive labels are clickable and dimmed while the active label is neither: tabs.py:206-213 (active uses plain style; inactive carries @click meta and goes through Opacity).
Inactive label meta survives dimming because of the Opacity fix at opacity.py:43.

Bar click zones use the padded span: tabs.py:90-92 selection_range, passed through tabs.py:219-222. The reference computes selection ranges after advancing its cursor (reference tabs.py:140-146), which yields (4, 9) for the first ' One ' label at tab_padding=1 instead of (0, 5). The candidate's ranges are the intended ones; a test pinned to the reference numbers would disagree.

Keyboard behavior: digit and 0 handling (tabs.py:417-433), left/right wrap (tabs.py:~381-394), first-character search that starts after the active tab and skips it (tabs.py:396-415), Escape (tabs.py:354).
Default active tab is set by name (tabs.py:300-305). The reference assigns a Tab object there (reference tabs.py:217), so the reference shows no active style by default.
Duplicate names display once at the first position with the last label (tabs.py:142-151), matching the reference behavior.
Zero-width early path returns before click spans (underline_bar.py:57-59), the same as the reference, so this is parity rather than a regression.

Deliberate divergence: first-character search compares only tab.label[:1] (tabs.py:~417 area), so multi-character key names such as 'enter' cannot match, while the reference uses startswith. The candidate is closer to the documented 'type a character' intent.
criteria.deficiency: Non-blocking edge defect, not a blocker: _highlight_range (tabs.py:176-185) indexes the de-duplicated displayed layouts with a full-list index from find_tab_by_name. Example: tabs [A, B(x), C(x), D] with D active gives displayed [A, C(x), D] and index 3 % 3 = 0, so the bar sits under A. The reference has the same index mismatch (reference tabs.py:155) and raises IndexError in that case, so this is shared with the reference rather than a regression. Duplicate names are a documented edge case.
